claims.text: Combining ab initio phonon calculations with machine learning will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than traditional models.
The integrated approach will improve predictive accuracy by at least 30% relative to traditional models.
The relevant high-entropy alloys can be synthesized with a controlled, homogeneous microstructure.
The model combines ab initio phonon-simulation outputs with statistical relationships based on composition and disorder-induced scattering parameters.
Optimized processing conditions can ensure both uniform microstructure and stability from cryogenic to moderate temperatures.
Composition-derived disorder profiles tune phonon-scattering behavior.
Chemical composition, microstructural disorder, and phonon scattering have complex interactions that can be captured by machine learning.
Ab initio calculations provide accurate descriptions of local lattice dynamics.
Adding ab initio descriptions of local lattice dynamics enables statistical learning to predict thermal-transport properties more accurately.
The model will predict low phonon thermal conductivity with more than a 30% improvement in accuracy over conventional models.
Traditional predictive approaches use simplified scattering estimates or phenomenological models without integrated ab initio data.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys with minimal microstructural inhomogeneity.
The approach is applicable only over temperature ranges in which the alloy phase remains stable.
Predictive improvement will vary with the amount of available experimental data and with the alloy system.
Temperature can materially affect phase stability in a high-entropy alloy.
Laser-flash analysis or the 3ω method can be used to measure thermal conductivity for the benchmark.
Failure to reduce prediction error by at least 30% relative to conventional models would falsify the hypothesis.
A lack of significant correlation between disorder profiles and measured phonon scattering would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and falsification rule use an improvement threshold of at least 30%, whereas the predicted outcome requires more than 30%. An outcome of exactly 30% would satisfy the former threshold but not the latter.
